## Function Disassemble

disassemble(code: bytes) -> list of (pc, op, arg) tuples, one per instruction, in code order: pc is the byte offset, op the opcode byte (int), arg the immediate bytes of PUSH1..PUSH32 (0x60..0x7f, n = op - 0x5f bytes) and b"" for every other opcode.

Behaviour: Every byte that is not a PUSH immediate is an instruction, including undefined opcodes (no name table, no validation). A PUSH whose immediate runs past the end of the code takes the bytes that are there (a shorter arg) and ends the list; nothing raises. Empty code gives []. PUSH0 (0x5f) has no immediate.

- reads: Runtime Code
- produces: Instruction

## Function Flag Risk

risk_flags(code: bytes) -> {"selfdestruct": bool, "mutable_delegatecall": bool}: two per-code security flags read from the runtime bytecode alone -- no source, no data-flow, no control-flow graph.

Behaviour: Both flags are read from the disassembly of the body from strip_metadata, so a 0xFF or 0xF4 byte inside a PUSH immediate or inside the metadata trailer never counts. selfdestruct is True when an opcode SELFDESTRUCT (0xFF) appears in that body: it marks the opcode present as an executable instruction, not a proof that some path reaches it (there is no CFG here, only disassembly). mutable_delegatecall is True when four conditions hold together: an opcode DELEGATECALL (0xF4) appears in the body, detect_proxy(code) is not "eip1167" (an EIP-1167 clone bakes its implementation address into the code and is excluded, however it is reached), an opcode SLOAD (0x54) appears in the body -- the cheap syntactic stand-in, since data-flow is out of scope, for an implementation address that comes from storage rather than hardcoded -- and is_std_proxy(code) is False: a standard EIP-1967/UUPS/Beacon proxy reads its implementation from an audited, well-known slot and is upgradeable by design, not a suspicious mutable delegatecall, so it is excluded even though it has DELEGATECALL and SLOAD. Order and position of the opcodes do not matter, only their presence. Never raises on empty or garbage bytes: risk_flags(b"") is both False.

- calls: Disassemble
- calls: Strip Metadata
- calls: Detect Proxy
- calls: Standard Proxy
